full.description: This image is a transmission electron micrograph showing the ultrastructure of a cell, specifically highlighting the basal lamina and surrounding cellular structures. The micrograph displays numerous mitochondria interspersed among deep infoldings of the basal plasma membrane, which is a characteristic feature of ion-transporting epithelia such as renal tubular cells. The basal lamina is clearly indicated by arrows adjacent to the plasma membrane infoldings. The high magnification allows for the detailed visualization of these specialized subcellular adaptations involved in active transport processes.

random.description: This is an electron micrograph showing an ultrastructural view of a renal tubule cell. The image highlights basal infoldings of the plasma membrane closely associated with numerous elongated mitochondria, which provide energy for active transport. The basal lamina is visible on the external surface of the epithelial cell. This characteristic morphology is typically seen in cells specialized for fluid and electrolyte reabsorption, such as those in the proximal or distal convoluted tubules of the kidney.
